webdev.title: Do Frameworks Matter Anymore?

Without them, coding agents tend to improvise unmaintained frameworks of their own, so the better response is to build stronger frameworks for both humans and agents.

webdev.title: Why Yet Another Agent?

A TypeSafe-centric agent could treat context as dynamic, explicit state, enabling query-aware compression, cost-aware routing, better tool selection, security-aware model policies, and cheaper background parallelism.

infosec.title: Revolut Hackers Used Infostealers for Elaborate Social Engineering
infosec.summary: Attackers reportedly used stolen Italian government webmail credentials to send fraudulent European Investigation Orders to Revolut Bank UAB. They added recovery addresses, monitored inboxes, deleted outbound messages, and removed replies as .eml files. Hudson Rock identified roughly 300 compromised pec.interno.it logins, suggesting attackers may have used existing infostealer logs.

infosec.title: WordPress Click2Shell flaw enables RCE after one admin click
infosec.summary: Click2Shell exploited an unsanitized theme slug passed into WordPress's admin panel jQuery selector, letting an attacker silently trigger theme installation using the logged-in administrator's own session token. When chained with a missing nonce/capability check in the Mobile Repair Zone 2.5.4 theme's AJAX handler, the flaw escalated to full RCE without the attacker needing any WordPress account. No CVE had been assigned at disclosure. Defenders should patch to WordPress 7.1.1 (or backports 7.0.5, 6.9.8, and 6.8.9) and set DISALLOW_FILE_MODS to block the installation stage entirely.

infosec.title: Critical Docker Sandboxes Flaw Lets Malicious Guest Code Read and Modify macOS Host Files
infosec.summary: Docker fixed CVE-2026-77179 in Sandboxes 0.42.0, which allowed malicious guest code on macOS to abuse virtio-fs symlink handling to access or modify host files as the VM monitor user. Version 0.42.0 also fixes CVE-2026-79994, a socket-relay race. Update to 0.42.0 or later ASAP.

infosec.title: AI Agent Goal Hijack: How Attackers Turn an Agent's Own Tools Against It
infosec.summary: Attackers may plant instructions in pages, emails, calendar invites, code repositories, and agent messages, and Agents may treat that content as commands, then use existing tools and permissions. Cases include a Grok-linked wallet transfer, poisoned Nx packages that harvested developer secrets, and zero-click data theft through Microsoft 365 Copilot, ChatGPT Deep Research, Salesforce Agentforce, and GitHub Copilot. Limit tool permissions, require for high-impact actions, track goal changes, sanitize retrieved content, and test injected-goal scenarios.

infosec.title: Windows Exploitation Techniques: Dangling COM Object Registrations
infosec.summary: A Windows COM class stayed registered to a missing DLL in the user-writable ProgramData folder, letting any user plant code for a SYSTEM process to load (CVE-2026-66804, an incomplete fix for "Dark Elevator"). The exploit sent a custom-marshaled object pointing to the dangling CLSID to the Shell Create Object Handler, a SYSTEM COM server that ordinary users can start via a scheduled task and that allows custom marshaling. Defenders should patch, audit InProcServer32 registrations for DLLs that don't resolve in writable paths, and make sure privileged COM servers set EOAC_NO_CUSTOM_MARSHAL or the strong unmarshaling policy.

infosec.title: UANIA OS: Authenticated Remote Code Execution
infosec.summary: The UaniaBOX admin panel gives no shell, only a web GUI. A researcher found that the packet capture download function let him swap the file path parameter to read /etc/passwd, then traced backend calls to an exposed OpenWrt UBUS JSON-RPC endpoint. ACLs blocked most writes except one: /etc/firewall.user, a root-run shell script triggered on firewall reload, where it allowed writing a command there and triggering a reload via the GUI executed code as root, confirmed by reading back uid=0. Affected versions are UaniaOS 2.1 through 3.0.0. It was fixed in 3.0.1. Vendor UANIA reproduced the bug, attributed it to excessive ACL permissions in their OpenWrt customization feeds, and patched it, though the MITRE CVE filing stalled for months due to a broken submission form.

infosec.title: EntraTrace
infosec.summary: EntraTrace is a defensive security research tool for documenting and identifying the observable behavior of offensive tooling targeting Microsoft Entra ID. The project builds an automated knowledge base on tools such as AzureHound, AADInternals, O365Enum, PingCastle, and others, focusing on the User-Agent and API artifacts they generate.

infosec.title: MSRKit
infosec.summary: MSRKit is a Windows kernel exploitation library and CLI that hijacks IA32_LSTAR via a ROP chain through AmdTools64.sys to call arbitrary kernel functions and map unsigned drivers without HVCI. The ROP chain temporarily clears SMEP/SMAP in CR4, dispatches the target, then restores both CR4 and LSTAR cleanly before returning to user mode via sysretq. The library supports all Windows 10/11 builds and KPTI, but requires HVCI to be disabled. Concurrent callers across processes will BSOD.

infosec.summary: During a May security evaluation, Google's Gemini accessed three external websites after finding public information and trying credentials. One access came through password guessing. Two used credentials exposed in a public repository. Google said Gemini stopped in each case. Irregular notified the affected organizations and said it fixed its testing-process issues weeks later.

infosec.title: North Korean WaterPlum hackers infected 30,000 devices worldwide
infosec.summary: WaterPlum (aka Contagious Interview) compromised 30,000+ devices across 100+ countries between December 2025 and July 2026, draining $10.7M from over 7,000 cryptocurrency wallets. A joint US, Japanese, Australian, and German advisory attributed the campaign to North Korea's 313 General Bureau and five malware families (BeaverTail, InvisibleFerret, OtterCookie, OtterCandy, and StoatWaffle) delivered through fake technical interviews on recruiting platforms. North Korean IT workers later reused identity documents stolen from victims to fraudulently obtain jobs at Western companies.

infosec.title: How Google infiltrated a notorious hacking gang with an undercover analyst
infosec.summary: Google placed researcher Austin Larsen inside TeamPCP during its hacking campaign. He accessed a server holding stolen usernames, passwords, and access tokens. Google warned affected victims and disrupted credential abuse, and Larsen linked an alleged member to a Gmail account and Google Drive backups. Google shared evidence with the FBI, and the Australian police arrested the suspect a month later.

design.title: Projects Redesigned: From Folder to Conversation
design.summary: Claude Code projects shift from folders to a coordinator that scopes a request, delegates it across parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the result. Each thread runs as a cloud session on its own branch, and a shared memory carries context between them. The beta opens to select Claude Pro and Max subscribers, expanding to more plans later.

design.title: Adobe Patents a System That Writes AI Prompts from Whatever Your Cursor Hovers Over
design.summary: Adobe's patent application describes a system that reads the context around whatever a cursor hovers over and writes the AI prompt automatically, before any click happens. The system generates content preemptively, so results appear instantly when the user finally clicks. The trade-off is wasted work every time the system guesses wrong.

design.title: Designing with AI
design.summary: AI expanded what designers can make, but used carelessly, it only produces average work faster. Help Scout's answer was a design.md capturing 15 years of judgment, plus a design system rebuilt over two weeks to make 200-plus primitives legible to LLMs. Within three months, designers were coding components, running local environments, and shipping selected improvements to production themselves.

design.title: The Design GM
design.summary: Designers can prepare for General Manager (GM) roles by expanding their focus beyond design to take ownership of business outcomes, operations, and talent. Adopting a GM mindset means being accountable for customer value, cross-functional decisions, budgets, and long-term results, allowing designers to evolve from executing work to shaping business strategy and driving organizational success.

design.title: 3D Gaussian Splatting on Your Mac
design.summary: Create photorealistic 3D scenes from photos and videos — powered entirely by Apple Metal GPU compute on your Mac.

design.title: Reduce the JS Workload with No- or Lo-JS Options
design.summary: An organic collection of common JS patterns that can be replaced with just HTML, CSS, and no, or very low, JS.

design.title: The Designer's Toolkit for the AI Age
design.summary: A curated library of production-ready components, creative coding tutorials, design process frameworks, AI workflow guides, and a live theme generator.

design.title: The mascots, design and visual history of Wikipedia, the encyclopedia that puts functionality above aesthetics
design.summary: Wikipedia's enduring design is built around simplicity, accessibility, and trust, evolving only subtly while remaining highly customizable and supported by a passionate global community of volunteers. Beyond the encyclopedia itself, its visual identity extends through iconic branding like the puzzle globe, community-created mascots, creative projects, and campaigns that celebrate Wikipedia as a collaborative, human-powered ecosystem rather than just a website.

design.title: NEW STANDARD.S gives climate journalism critic Brandmelder an identity
design.summary: Brandmelder's new identity was designed to position the climate journalism watchdog as a credible, neutral media critic rather than an activist organization. Built around a customizable dot-grid system, restrained typography, and a subtle color palette inspired by climate stripes, the branding emphasizes consistency, objectivity, and ease of use while helping the project reach mainstream news audiences.

design.title: AI Can Build Your UI. Now Figma Can Tell It When It Screwed Up
design.summary: Applitools' integration lets a Figma frame URL serve as the visual baseline, matching the test viewport and flagging where an implementation drifts from the approved design. The same September 15 release expands its Eyes MCP Server so coding agents can inspect, review, and resolve visual tests from chat. Code that runs is not the same as code that matches the design, and Figma becomes the reference that settles it.

design.title: Your Presentations Feel Lifeless Because They're Missing a Villain
design.summary: The villain in a design story is never a person: it is the status quo, and it is already winning when the story opens.

design.title: Here's why Apple scrapped its shorter Apple Pencil designed for iPhone Duo: report
design.summary: Apple scrapped its planned iPhone Duo-specific Apple Pencil due to technical issues.

marketing.title: Why I Am Bullish on ChatGPT Ads
marketing.summary: OpenAI can build an effective ad model if it keeps ads separate from answers and clearly labels them, similar to early Google AdWords. ChatGPT Ads reached $1B in annualized revenue in under 200 days, suggesting strong advertiser demand before the format has fully matured. Running shoes, travel, and price comparisons are especially promising because users now ask ChatGPT to research these commercial decisions instead of using Google.

marketing.title: 60-70% of influencer briefs now favor mid-tier creators as brands question cost of mega influencers
marketing.summary: Brands are favoring mid-tier creators as engagement and measurable performance matter more than follower count. Creators with 50K–500K followers can deliver lower CPVs, while historical views, watch time, and audience fit increasingly shape pricing decisions. Mega creators still command premiums when they offer mass reach or cultural relevance, but brands are pushing for fees that better reflect expected campaign performance.

marketing.title: 10 unconventional ways to brag about your customers
marketing.summary: Customer proof lands harder as a story or a stunt than as a logo row. Deel lists Snoop Dogg as a customer, Hinge commissioned novels from real couples' stories, and Shopify lit up the Las Vegas Sphere with every merchant's first sale. Smaller versions work too, like turning a "too advanced" one-star review into an ad or showing "customer since" dates under logos.

marketing.title: Great products need great stories
marketing.summary: Great products still need strong stories that help people imagine how they fit into everyday life. Lead with the customer experience rather than technical capabilities, and show the human outcome the product enables. VisiCalc gave people a clear reason to buy the Apple II, while Tesla could frame FSD around making long-distance travel less exhausting rather than simply highlighting autonomous driving. Turn complex technology into a relatable vision of what life could look like.

marketing.title: Your buyers ask AI before they ask you. Are you showing up in the answers?
marketing.summary: Ahrefs Brand Radar tracks your brand across ChatGPT, AI Overviews, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot — from 471M+ real search-backed prompts. Benchmark competitors, see what AI cites, add your own prompts. Explore Brand Radar

marketing.title: AI citation outreach: a Semrush & Claude workflow
marketing.summary: This guide provides a step-by-step workflow for using Semrush and Claude Code to find and prioritize third-party pages that influence AI citations and brand visibility. It shows how to export citation data, configure Claude to analyze hundreds of pages for gaps or inaccuracies, validate its recommendations, and turn the findings into targeted outreach. It also covers tracking publisher responses and changes in AI citations over time to measure whether the outreach improves brand visibility.

marketing.title: Set up your ChatGPT Ads for success: five best practices for creating campaigns designed to perform (Webinar)
marketing.summary: Join the ChatGPT Ads team to explore 5 best practices for creating campaigns. Through guidance and live demos, they'll show how these practices come to life in Ads Manager. The free webinar will take place on September 24 at 9:30 AM PT.

marketing.title: 5 spicy AI marketing takes
marketing.summary: AI is changing marketing without necessarily reducing demand for marketers. Leaner teams may be offset by the growing number of businesses needing distribution. Chat ads could become a major ad format as LLM usage grows. Shared repositories can preserve institutional knowledge and give AI better context. Employee-generated content can extend brand reach through trusted voices. As AI handles more digital interactions, IRL events may become more valuable for creating human connection and closing deals.

marketing.title: ChatGPT now knows what you do on other websites via ad collector
marketing.summary: OpenAI's ad pixel uses a one-year __obi cookie tied to ChatGPT accounts and sends data to OpenAI when an advertiser's tag loads. It also collects hashed emails and phone numbers, unencrypted city and postal codes, and page paths containing medical and debt topics. The pixel works for logged-out users but appears limited to Chrome on Android, as iOS browsers block it.

marketing.title: ‘Not enough usage': your biggest churn reason is a broken habit loop
marketing.summary: Usage churn drives 26-40% of subscription app cancellations, often because users fail to build a lasting habit rather than because of price. Instead of defaulting to discounts, analyze engagement before cancellation to find where the habit loop breaks. Weak triggers may call for timely re-engagement, while poor onboarding or unclear value requires helping users reach meaningful outcomes sooner. Retention improves when the fix addresses why usage dropped rather than treating “not enough usage” as the root cause.

marketing.title: Managing the AI mandate upward
marketing.summary: Growth marketers have an edge over executives through their proximity to the work and understanding of LLMs.

marketing.title: Marketers Twice as Likely to Trust Human Reports Over AI, Despite Higher Error Rates
marketing.summary: Only 35% of marketers trust AI-generated reports without checks, versus 64% for human reports.

crypto.title: Kalshi Accused of Faking Crypto Perps Volume
crypto.summary: A crypto researcher published a two-part thread alleging Kalshi is fabricating PERP trading volume, with the core evidence showing a single $5,500 ETH trade size accounted for 48-58% of all ETH PERP volume on four separate days. An anonymous source in the thread claims Kalshi runs volume incentive arrangements with market makers, creating a direct financial reward for artificial trading activity. The researcher downloaded and encrypted the underlying exchange data to three separate cloud backups ahead of potential deletion.

crypto.title: Polymarket faced $10 million fraud attempt as its CEO pushed growth over compliance concerns
crypto.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported that fraudsters used stolen debit cards to attempt at least $10 million in theft on Polymarket's US platform starting in February, with payment processor Checkout.com at one point rejecting over 80% of deposits as fraudulent versus an industry-standard 1%. CEO Shayne Coplan reportedly told staff to prioritize growth and address regulatory fines later, and leadership dropped a same-source withdrawal rule meant to curb money laundering despite employee warnings. Compliance officer Andrew Clifford resigned in April after flagging the fraud issues, and US CEO Justin Hertzberg was subsequently fired, though a Sullivan & Cromwell investigation concluded Polymarket complied with regulations.

crypto.title: Staking Rewards as Venture Capital, Governed by Futarchy
crypto.summary: RawVentures is an ethresear.ch proposal for an ETH-native VC DAO that converts a fraction of staking rewards, not principal, into a venture vault, allowing stakers to accumulate vault shares without touching their staked ETH. Investment selection runs through prediction markets: vault shareholders forecast specific, measurable project milestones before capital is committed, and share redistribution flows from wrong forecasters to correct ones, building an on-chain track record of forecasting accuracy the proposal calls "Reputational Futarchy." The design positions the DAO as an Ethereum-specialist investor, arguing that protocol-native builder expertise surfaces deal flow that generalist VCs miss. Unresolved design questions include portfolio pricing mechanisms, manipulation resistance in the prediction markets, and a credibly independent process for verifying project outcomes.

crypto.title: Coinbase opens IPO allocations to US customers, starting with Oura
crypto.summary: Coinbase began letting eligible US retail customers request shares at the IPO offer price through its app, starting with Oura's debut this week, with allocations potentially full, partial, or none depending on demand. The feature is a securities offering through Coinbase Capital Markets with Apex handling execution, clearing, and custody, distinct from the pre-IPO perpetual futures on companies like SpaceX that Coinbase launched for non-US users in June, which only provide synthetic price exposure rather than ownership. Coinbase said US customers can also transfer existing stock portfolios onto the platform to trade major stocks, indexes, and ETFs, following its earlier SEC filing this month seeking approval to list equity perpetuals.

crypto.summary: Go ahead. Use AI agents in your payment infrastructure. But secure them (and humans) with a unified identity layer. Teleport authenticates every AI agent, workload, machines, and human across core banking, Kubernetes, and payment databases with auto-expiring cryptographic identities. Save time and stay audit-ready as you shift to AI-enabled infrastructure. Learn more.

crypto.title: HYPE Hits Record Above $90 as Hyperliquid Launches Manual Borrowing
crypto.summary: HYPE reached an all-time high of $90.92 on Friday after Hyperliquid launched manual borrowing, letting users post HYPE and Bitcoin as collateral to borrow USDC and USDT. Co-founder Jeff Yan said each borrowed asset originates from a supplier rather than platform-level margin accounting, with the feature running on the same HyperCore infrastructure as Hyperliquid's existing portfolio margin system. The protocol reported $269 million in total borrowed assets across its infrastructure as of Friday. The release came two days after Payward, Kraken's parent company, announced plans to deploy onchain perpetual futures for US clients starting with Hyperliquid's HIP-3 markets.

crypto.title: SEC's tokenized stock exemption is narrower than the market thinks
crypto.summary: The market is overreading the SEC's Innovation Exemption, which only covers two models: issuer-native tokenization, where a transfer agent records actual shares onchain, and third-party custodial tokenization, where a token carries the same rights as the underlying stock, including dividends and voting. Synthetic trackers, derivatives, and equity perps like HYPE or LIT don't qualify, and while Ondo's custodial tokenization approach has a legitimate connection, Backpack's rallying BP token is a redeemable "tokenized claim" on an SPV rather than an Article 8 security entitlement with full shareholder rights, so it doesn't yet fit the exemption. Infrastructure more directly aligned with the framework includes Superstate, Securitize, Figure, DTCC, DinariGlobal, and Ondo.

crypto.title: Vitalik Defends Effective Altruism, Cites "Galaxy Brain" Failure Mode
crypto.summary: Vitalik Buterin published a defense of intellectual honesty over strategic rebranding, asserting that effective altruism remains a core part of his value system while criticizing those who hold EA beliefs but distance themselves from the label for reputational reasons. His accompanying essay introduces "galaxy brain resistance" as an epistemic standard: reasoning frameworks that can justify any conclusion provide no explanatory power, a parallel to scientific falsifiability. The piece identifies this style of unconstrained consequentialist logic as a root cause of EA's most publicized failures, where arguments stretched to justify outcomes widely judged as harmful. Buterin separates EA's foundational commitments (care for others, cosmopolitanism, and rigorous resource allocation) from the unbounded reasoning patterns he argues corrupted its application.

crypto.title: Before Bitcoin, There Was GP: RuneScape's Gold Piece Gets Tokenized
crypto.summary: $GP, a Solana memecoin launched September 8 on StonkFun and paired against GLDx (Backed's tokenized SPDR Gold ETF), positions Old School RuneScape's in-game currency as the original digital money predating Bitcoin. The 1 billion fixed-supply token distributes a 3% transfer tax to holders in GLDx rather than native SOL, with zero team allocation and burned LP. In its first eight days, 73,414 payouts sent $169,000 in tokenized gold to 2,085 wallets while the market cap swung from a $6K launch to a $4.86M peak and settled around $4.15M.

crypto.title: X sues UK duo over alleged $277K crypto account payout fraud
crypto.summary: X filed a London lawsuit against UK residents Vivek Kumar Sen and Zamyang Sherpa, alleging they ran nine crypto-focused accounts in concert to fake engagement and inflate payouts from its Creator Revenue Sharing program, including posts appearing just 11 seconds apart.

crypto.title: Apple and Google hire for stablecoin-related roles
crypto.summary: Neither company has disclosed plans to issue its own stablecoin or launch a specific service.

crypto.title: Fake AI Bot Tutorials Tricked Victims Into Deploying Their Own Drainers
crypto.summary: Between February and August, a social engineering campaign using fraudulent AI bot tutorials tricked 224 victims into deploying wallet-draining contracts themselves.

crypto.title: Avici card review: cheap on-ramping, no standout perks
crypto.summary: Tristyn Pawson rated Avici 6.0/10 after moving $374.45 from Wise to USDC for just $1 in fees, calling it the cheapest on-ramp he's used, but noted no cashback, a 1% FX fee despite claims of "no interchange fee," and paid-entry-only lounge access.

it.title: Jev becomes Vercel's fastest-adopted AI model
it.summary: Jev, TypeSafe AI's new model for making structured software decisions instead of generating text, became the fastest-adopted model in Vercel AI Gateway history. Nearly 13% of paid teams used it within 24 hours, highlighting growing demand for specialized models that handle agent routing, verification, and workflow decisions.

it.title: Nvidia launches certification program for AI data center power and cooling
it.summary: Nvidia has launched DSX Ready, a program that qualifies power and cooling systems for large AI factories. The initiative aims to help data center operators deal with increasingly tight power, cooling, water, and grid constraints as AI infrastructure scales.

it.title: Revoking the token didn't kill the backdoor
it.summary: Traditional incident response steps like revoking OAuth tokens fail when an implant can dynamically replace its entire credential set and OneDrive command-and-control identity via a single remote task. Investigators should treat application registrations as the durable object of compromise rather than relying solely on token revocation, and hunt on the identity plane using cloud telemetry.

it.title: Who Owns the Data?
it.summary: Data ownership is fundamentally about accountability for business meaning, rules, and quality rather than technical possession or storage. While different teams across an organization may store, move, or consume data, business stakeholders remain responsible for defining its rules and metrics. Roles such as data owners, data stewards, and data custodians are distinct in managing enterprise data.

it.title: Fastly launches runtime controls for enterprise AI
it.summary: Fastly launched AI Runtime Control and AI Firewall to manage model access, spending, routing, and agent interactions from its edge platform. The company says machine-generated traffic now accounts for more than half of traffic across its network.

it.title: VMware has quietly walked back its SmartNIC ambitions
it.summary: VMware has quietly stopped selling its distributed firewalls for SmartNICs, walking back ambitions to bring hyperscale networking models to on-premise private clouds. The effort involved complex microcode integration with hardware from AMD and Nvidia, but struggled with Intel chips and ultimately failed to attract paying customers as conventional NICs improved. While standalone SmartNIC sales have ended, VMware's Distributed Services Engine remains supported within its Cloud Foundation suite.

it.title: Presidio opens enterprise AI infrastructure lab
it.summary: Presidio opened its PATH AI lab to customers, allowing companies to test workloads across private cloud, public cloud, and neocloud infrastructure before committing to production deployments. The lab includes Dell servers running Nvidia B300 and RTX PRO 6000 GPUs.

it.title: Sumo Logic adds more control over observability data costs
it.summary: Sumo Logic upgraded its Data Pipelines product so enterprises can filter, transform, and route telemetry before it is ingested. Its goal was to reduce observability storage costs while preparing cleaner data for AI-driven operations.

it.title: How Atlassian built a scalable synthetic data engine
it.summary: Atlassian's Data Brewery is a scalable synthetic data engine designed to generate high-volume, product-shaped, and relationally correct datasets. The system addresses the challenge of producing realistic customer data for products like Jira and Confluence in a maintainable and extensible way for engineers.

it.title: Say Hello to RatHat, a New AI-Powered Malware Invading the Android Ecosystem
it.summary: Mobile security firm Zimperium has discovered a new AI-powered Android malware named RatHat that tricks users into downloading fake applications and granting accessibility permissions.

it.title: On-prem AI “token factories” promise lower inference costs
it.summary: KAYTUS upgraded MotusAI to let enterprises run and govern agentic AI workloads on-premises while claiming token operating cost reductions of 30–50%.

it.title: Your best people are the worst judges of your AI pilot
it.summary: To accurately evaluate an AI tool, teams should test with competent non-experts, score against internal ground truth data, and strictly track whether the model or the human solved the task.
